decisions.reason: The Statement explicitly asserts a relative-open cover of a strong deformation retract Y, not a three-dimensional open-ball cover of E_K. Steps 4.1 and 6.1 construct that retract and its open disks with annular overlaps; step 5.1 gives the free meridian region. Van Kampen applies in Y and the strong retraction transports its fundamental group. The title does not add a stronger mathematical hypothesis or conclusion.

Independent basing paths replace each meridian by an unrelated conjugate, which need not satisfy the listed crossing relator. The Definition now requires the common upper-collar paths of the local-conjugacy lemma, with a single shared stem from an arbitrary basepoint; the rational validation, traversal, symbols and output relators are unchanged.

F2 attributed the free-group attaching word to a supplier that states meridian conjugacy in the completed complement. That equality alone cannot identify the kernel for van Kampen. Step 2.1 now computes the cap-boundary loop in U: the two-holed top plate gives ms eta mt^-1 eta^-1; common collar access gives alpha_s eta alpha_t^-1=mo in the upper region, hence ms mo mt^-1 mo^-1, a conjugate of the emitted relator (up to inversion). No attached cap is used in this computation. Statement unchanged.

The cited supplier proof actually constructs exactly the vertical-slab convex-cell face-to-face triangulation, in steps 1.1–4.1; F6 accurately describes this supplied construction, even though its Statement records only existence. No unsupplied construction is being imported. The finite face-disk extension is given locally in step 2.1. Exact rational recomputation confirms all 276 pairs (40 declared endpoint intersections, 236 disjoint, no overlaps), all four determinants and side tests, and the closed-three-braid visit sequence. The relator redundancy follows by the displayed cancellation. The algorithm access-path correction is compatible with the explicit common-collar hypothesis already in this Statement.

F7 cited only the definition of [G,G] for the abelianization quotient, although the correct universal-abelianization theorem was already declared as F8. Corrected F7 to the actual commutator definition and F8 to the quotient plus universal property; step 1.1 now explicitly proves [Z,Z]=1 and invokes F8, and step 2.1 uses F8. The counterexample remains sound: aba=bab abelianizes to a=b with an inverse map to Z, while the two transpositions satisfy the braid relation and generate nonabelian S3. Also supplied a finite rational polygonal code for the displayed three-crossing braid, making its invocation of the finite-code constructor explicit. Statement refuted unchanged; diagram arrows, three right-starting overpasses, labels, closure and (o,L,R) triples checked.
